title: Rig soak: three-camera sessions intermittently fail to open cameras (dshow I/O error) and a camera re-enumerates mid-series
body:
Evidence from 2026-09-06 evening on the lab rig (all cameras on the Sonnet root hub `9&1d291187`; cam_c two hub tiers deep behind the TS4, which was chained on the Sonnet contrary to runbook rule 3):

- Back-to-back three-camera `record` runs at 1920x1200@60 for 4 s: runs 1 and 2 supported (59.8/60.0/60.1 fps, 59.8/60.1/60.0 fps); runs 3-5 aborted at `plan-check` with `missing=['cam_b']`; run 6 (640x480@200) opened cam_a at 200.5 fps while cam_b and cam_c failed with `Error opening input files: I/O error` (rc -5) before delivering a frame.
- `DEVPKEY_Device_LastArrivalDate` shows `USB\VID_32E4&PID_5234\2605160001` re-arrived at 20:50:23, i.e. one camera dropped off the bus and re-enumerated during the series.
- The earlier 10-mode sweep showed the same pattern: every three-camera run lost two cameras at open (rc -5, 0 bytes) while the single-camera runs of the same modes succeeded; a later three-camera run at 60 fps then succeeded 3/3.
- Solo opens of each camera succeed; 1600x1200@120 opens and decodes zero frames (`I/O error` during demuxing).

Since the fix in the flexibility PR, `recordings.json` carries `recorder_note` (ffmpeg's last stderr) and `recorder_wall_s`, and a zero-frame recording is `blocked`, so the failure is at least named. Still unknown: whether the TS4-behind-Sonnet chain, USB power on the Sonnet, or the DirectShow graph race is the cause.

Acceptance: 10 consecutive three-camera `record` runs at 1920x1200@60 with the TS4 on its own Thunderbolt port and every camera directly on a Sonnet jack, all `supported`, no re-enumeration in `LastArrivalDate`; then repeat with the TS4 chained to reproduce or clear rule 3. Consider a `record --repeat N` soak mode that records this evidence automatically. Part of #9599 / #9422.
